summary: Solid T1 module: AXFR + NSEC walk + SPF/DMARC absence are all deterministic-if-vulnerable probes with parsed evidence (leaked names). CVE gating on BIND is absent (version.bind is fingerprint-only). No T2/T3 activity — the module never chains AXFR data into hostname/target injection for downstream scanners as a first-class handoff (currently just extra strings in the report). Biggest gap: no DNS cache-injection probe / recursion-open detection / SIG(0)+TSIG bypass — and no CVE gate on version.bind for known BIND CVEs (2020-8617/8623/8625).

findings.tier_evidence: AXFR succeeds only when the server actually allows the transfer; recce parses and samples the RR names as evidence.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-inject leaked A/AAAA records as known_hosts + hostnames into the shared discovery surface so downstream scanners (SMB/LDAP/kerb/HTTP) pivot immediately; also add CVE gate for BIND named CVE-2020-8617/8623 by parsing version.bind alongside.
findings.tester_next_step: dig AXFR <zone> @<ip> +tcp; ingest hostnames/IPs into scope, then run: crackmapexec smb <new_ips> --gen-relay-list relay.txt; kerbrute userenum -d <zone> users.txt --dc <ip>.

findings.title_pattern: DNS zone enumerated via NSEC walk ({zone})
findings.tier_evidence: NSEC record chain is walked and names captured — presence proves the misconfig.
findings.promotion_notes: Fold NSEC-derived names into the shared hostname surface same as AXFR; add NSEC3 walker (hashcat -m 8300) as tester_next_step so hashed zones can also be cracked offline.
findings.tester_next_step: ldns-walk <zone> @<ip>; for NSEC3: nsec3walker <zone> then hashcat -m 8300 nsec3.hashes rockyou.txt to recover the hashed labels.

findings.tier_evidence: TXT lookup returns no v=spf1 — deterministic evidence of the config gap.
findings.promotion_notes: Add active spoof-test probe: attempt SMTP MAIL FROM: <spoofed@zone> to a discovered MX and record whether the MTA accepts — proves exploitability. Gated behind --safe-off since it hits real inboxes.
findings.tester_next_step: swaks --to test@<zone> --from ceo@<zone> --server <mx> --header 'Subject: spoof test'  # proves receiving MTA accepts unsigned spoofed mail.

findings.tier_evidence: TXT record is present but contains +all/?all — regex match on parsed value.
findings.promotion_notes: Same as dns_missing_spf: add live spoof-delivery test through the discovered MX.
findings.tester_next_step: swaks --to test@<zone> --from spoof@<zone> --server <mx>; check whether SPF-failing mail lands in Inbox.

findings.tier_evidence: _dmarc.<zone> TXT lookup returned empty — confirmed absence.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain with SPF spoof test for full DMARC-bypass proof; add DKIM missing-selector detection to raise severity.
findings.tester_next_step: swaks --to victim@<zone> --from ceo@<zone> --server <mx>  # DMARC absent => spoofed From: passes end-to-end.

findings.tier_evidence: Regex hit on p=none in the actual DMARC record.
findings.tester_next_step: swaks --to victim@<zone> --from cfo@<zone> --server <mx>; delivery to Inbox proves monitor-only enforcement.

findings.tier_evidence: Pure discovery — presence of _ldap._tcp + _kerberos._tcp SRV records.
findings.promotion_notes: Consume as a shared known_domains + known_dc_targets surface so LDAP/Kerberos/SMB modules auto-target the DCs, and emit a real T1 finding when the SRV target resolves to an internal RFC1918 address exposed externally.
findings.tester_next_step: kerbrute userenum -d <zone> --dc <dc_target> users.txt; ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<dc> -b DC=<zone_dc>,DC=<tld> '(objectClass=user)' sAMAccountName.

findings.tier_evidence: Fingerprint only — version.bind CH TXT response, no vulnerability probe.
findings.promotion_notes: Add a BIND CVE-gate table (like ntp's) — CVE-2020-8617/8623/8625/2021-25214/2022-38177 by parsed version. Low risk; version-match style.
findings.tester_next_step: dig CH TXT version.bind @<ip>; compare against ISC BIND security advisories; if <9.11.35 test with 'nmap --script dns-cache-snoop' for CVE-2020-8617.
